# Preface {.unnumbered}

This report describes a study of vocabulary development in children with Down syndrome. The study aims to characterise trajectories of word learning, spoken and gestured production, and relationships between words understood and produced. Our primary goal is to provide practical information that can accurately inform expectations, intervention and teaching practice.

We have tried to write this report for a broad audience of families, practitioners and researchers. We cannot avoid statistical and computational details, but we try to explain as much as we can for readers for whom aspects of these may not be familiar. For readers who would prefer a more concise overview, a summary report is also available, together with interactive tools for exploring the data and findings at [TODO: link].

To contribute to continuing progress, researchers should describe their methods and explain their results in sufficient detail for others to replicate their findings [@korbmacherReplicationCrisisHas2023; @mcelreathReplicationCommunicationPopulation2015]. These descriptions should include source code for statistical analyses that can be run using freely available software [@farrellComputationalModelingCognition2018; @mcelreathStatisticalRethinkingBayesian2020]. This is the goal of this report and the accompanying repository ([https://github.com/dseinternational/vocabulary-growth](https://github.com/dseinternational/vocabulary-growth)).

This study is not fixed in time. As new data becomes available, we anticipate updating our estimates and evolving our models. We will version the study, tagging releases in the repository whenever we publish updated analyses. We hope that "version 1.0" is helpful and of interest to families, practitioners and researchers alike, and welcome feedback, collaboration and contributions to future iterations.
